operators.meaning: Arithmetic on numeric operands: addition (+), subtraction (-), multiplication (*), division (/), and power (^). The result is a number expression, usable wherever a number is — most often one side of a comparison, e.g. [a] < [b] + 2.
constraints: operands must be numeric: number fields, numeric literals, Length, aggregates, or nested arithmetic
the result is a number, not a condition — wrap it in a comparison to form a rule's errorCondition

the power operator ^ may not be nested without grouping (a ^ b ^ c is rejected, MVK_TOO_MANY_POW_FOR_CALC); its exponent must be a whole number — a scale-0 field or an integer literal, never a decimal-scale field (MVK_INVALID_NUMBER_FOR_EXP)

gotchas.text: the symbols (+ - * / ^) are language-independent — identical in every condition language, not localized keywords

division by zero evaluates quietly: the condition becomes unknown (no fire), a computation computes nothing and clears a stale value; a bare division also has unknown scale — wrap it in RoundAccounting(expr, n) to assign to a scaled field
operator precedence is ^ first, then * and /, then + and -; group arithmetic sub-expressions with CURLY braces { } (e.g. 3 ^ {2 + 1}), not round or square brackets

the power a ^ b is not executed — so a rule using it silently does NOT fire — when the exponent is out of the range [-1000, 1000], or for 0 raised to a negative power; the same quiet behavior as division by zero

validExample.note: fires from the second line item onward (the error field under Items makes the rule iterate)

invalidExample.fix: CurrentRepetition needs the rule to iterate over the group — put the error field inside Items

operators.meaning: Delegates the fire/don't-fire decision to host code the consuming system registers under the given name — the escape hatch when the language cannot express a check.
constraints: the name is a bare identifier (letter, then letters/digits/underscores), no operands
forbidden inside a Having filter (MVK_DISALLOWED_CONSTRUCT_IN_FILTER_CONDITION) and in computation rules
does not satisfy the error-field rule on its own — pair it with a field reference

gotchas.text: the kernel only parses/places it; whether the registered implementation exists is the consuming system's concern, not checkConsistency's

validExample.note: host code decides; the FieldFilled conjunct references the error field

operators.meaning: The field's value in the repetition whose index field equals the given value ([Field For "value"]).
constraints: the field's enclosing repeatable group must declare an indexFieldName (else MVK_NO_INDEX_FIELD)
the index value is a string constant matching the index field; an iterating entity index is restricted (MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_INVALID_ITER)
accepted inside NumberOfFilledFields, but rejected inside NumberOfFilledGroups and RepetitionNotUnique (MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_NOT_ALLOWED)
not supported under a starred enclosing group (MVK_SEMANTIC_INDEX_AND_WILDCARD)

gotchas.text: selects a specific repetition by key — distinct from '*' (all repetitions) and the rule's own iteration
when no repetition carries the index value the comparison is not evaluated (no fire) — it does not fall back to the empty-number 0

validExample.note: the ordered count of the line item keyed SKU-1

invalidExample.fix: semantic index needs a repeatable group with an index field; BillingAddress has none

operators.meaning: The current date (ignores the time of day).
constraints: compares only to dates (a date field, another date expression) — not to numbers

gotchas.text: Now (the date-time sibling) is discouraged with == and forbidden in computations

validExample.note: fires when the order date is today or in the future

invalidExample.fix: Today compares to dates — compare a date field, not a number

operators.meaning: The number of whole days from the first date to the second.
constraints: both operands are dates (fields or date expressions), rendered as bare entity refs

gotchas.text: differences are a floor, not a calendar count (DifferenceInMonths(31.01,30.03)=1); fractional offsets truncate

validExample.note: fires when delivery is more than a week after order

operators.meaning: The largest number of whole months that can be added to the first date without passing the second.
constraints: both operands are dates

gotchas.text: a floor, not a calendar count (KERNEL-SEMANTICS §6)

validExample.note: fires when at least a month apart

operators.meaning: The largest number of whole years between the two dates.
constraints: both operands are dates

gotchas.text: a floor; a naive age check around leap days can be off (Add* vs Difference* disagree across leap years)

validExample.note: fires when at least a year apart

operators.meaning: The whole-hours difference between two date-times (second minus first).
constraints: both operands are date-times (fields or date-time expressions), rendered as bare entity refs

gotchas.text: a floor, not a rounded count; the sign follows operand order (DifferenceIn*(a,b) = b - a)

validExample.note: fires when completion is more than a day after scheduling

operators.meaning: The whole-minutes difference between two date-times (second minus first).
constraints: both operands are date-times

gotchas.text: a floor, not a rounded count

validExample.note: fires when more than 90 minutes elapsed

operators.meaning: The whole-seconds difference between two date-times (second minus first).
constraints: both operands are date-times

gotchas.text: a floor, not a rounded count

validExample.note: fires when completion is strictly after scheduling

operators.meaning: The date shifted forward by the given number of days.
constraints: the first operand is a date or date-time (bare entity ref); the second an integer amount

gotchas.text: fractional offsets are truncated, not rounded
over a date-time source AddDays shifts the day and preserves the time of day, returning a date-time; over a date it returns a date (AddYears/AddMonths/DifferenceInDays stay date-only)
on a date FRAGMENT, Add* is gated by the format's granularity — AddDays needs a day, AddMonths a month, AddYears a year, else MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP

validExample.note: fires when delivery is more than a week out

operators.meaning: The date shifted forward by the given number of months (preserves the day number).
constraints: the first operand is a date; the second an integer amount

gotchas.text: AddMonths preserves the day; AddYears maps end-of-February — they disagree across a leap-year boundary (§6)

validExample.note: fires when delivery is more than a quarter out

operators.meaning: The date shifted forward by the given number of years (maps end-of-February to end-of-February).
constraints: the first operand is a date; the second an integer amount

gotchas.text: differs from AddMonths across leap years (§6)

validExample.note: fires when delivery is more than a year out

operators.meaning: The date-time shifted by the given number of hours (may roll over the date; the amount may be negative).
constraints: the first operand is a date-time (bare entity ref); the second an integer amount

gotchas.text: operates on (and returns) a date-time, not a date — it can roll the calendar day over

validExample.note: the scheduled time, two hours on, is before 23:00

operators.meaning: The date-time shifted by the given number of minutes (amount may be negative).
constraints: the first operand is a date-time; the second an integer amount

gotchas.text: returns a date-time; can roll over the hour and day

validExample.note: the scheduled time, half an hour on

operators.meaning: The date-time shifted by the given number of seconds (amount may be negative).
constraints: the first operand is a date-time; the second an integer amount

gotchas.text: returns a date-time; can roll over the minute, hour and day

validExample.note: the scheduled time, 45 seconds on

operators.meaning: The year component of a date, as a number.
constraints: the operand is a date or date-time (a field or expression), rendered as a bare entity ref

validExample.note: fires for orders dated before 2020

operators.meaning: The month component of a date (1-12), as a number.
constraints: the operand is a date or date-time (a field or expression)

validExample.note: fires for December orders

operators.meaning: The day-of-month component of a date, as a number.
constraints: the operand is a date or date-time (a field or expression)

gotchas.text: rejected on a partially-known date (a DateType with a date precision other than FULL, e.g. DAY_OPTIONAL) — MVK_INVALID_DATE_TYPE; resolve it to a concrete date with ValueAsDate first. (MonthFromDate/YearFromDate/QuarterFromDate ARE permitted on a DAY_OPTIONAL date.)

validExample.note: fires for orders late in the month

operators.meaning: The calendar quarter of a date (1-4), as a number.
constraints: the operand is a date or date-time (a field or expression)

validExample.note: fires for fourth-quarter orders

operators.meaning: The start bound of a date-range field, as a comparable date.

gotchas.text: the operand is a BARE entity ref: StartOfDateRange(CoverageWindow), not StartOfDateRange([CoverageWindow]). Bracketing a function's argument is MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN — brackets are only for a field used as a comparison value.

constraints: the operand is a date-range field, rendered as a bare entity ref

validExample.note: fires when the coverage window starts after 2020

operators.meaning: The end bound of a date-range field, as a comparable date (feeds comparisons or DayFromDate/MonthFromDate/...).

gotchas.text: the operand is a BARE entity ref: EndOfDateRange(CoverageWindow), not EndOfDateRange([CoverageWindow]). Bracketing a function's argument is MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN — brackets are only for a field used as a comparison value.

constraints: the operand is a date-range field

validExample.note: fires when the coverage window ends late in the month

operators.meaning: True iff the date ranges of the listed date-range fields overlap (start and end inclusive).

gotchas.text: ranges are closed intervals: periods that merely TOUCH (one ends the day the other starts) overlap — seamless periods must start the day after the previous end

constraints: the operands are date-range fields (or a flattened repetition list of them)

validExample.note: fires when the order's coverage window overlaps a line-item coverage

operators.meaning: True iff the first date-range field's interval overlaps at least one date-range field in the list (start and end inclusive).

gotchas.text: ranges are closed intervals: periods sharing one boundary day count as overlapping

constraints: a date-range field, then In, then a date-range field list (often a flattened repetition list)

validExample.note: fires when the coverage window overlaps any line-item coverage

operators.meaning: The hour-of-day component (0-23) of a time or date-time, as a number.
constraints: the operand is a time or date-time (a field or expression), rendered as a bare entity ref

validExample.note: fires for pickups before 9am

operators.meaning: The minute component (0-59) of a time or date-time, as a number.
constraints: the operand is a time or date-time (a field or expression)

validExample.note: fires when the pickup minute is not on the hour

operators.meaning: The second component (0-59) of a time or date-time, as a number.
constraints: the operand is a time or date-time (a field or expression)

validExample.note: fires when the pickup time has no seconds offset

operators.meaning: The date part of a date-time, as a comparable date.
constraints: the operand is a date-time (a field or expression), rendered as a bare entity ref

validExample.note: fires when the scheduled date part is in the future

operators.meaning: The time-of-day part of a date-time, as a comparable time.
constraints: the operand is a date-time (a field or expression)

validExample.note: fires when the pickup time differs from the scheduled time part

operators.meaning: A substring of a string field's value, by character range (start, end). Typically feeds a string comparison or a concatenation.
constraints: the first operand is a string field; the two range bounds are integers — 1-based and inclusive, with start >= 1 and start <= end (MVK_INVALID_INTERVAL)

gotchas.text: an empty field or out-of-range bounds yield an empty string (not an error); like any string comparison the result is then not evaluated — guard with FieldFilled to fire only on present values

validExample.note: fires when the first three characters of the product code spell BAD

invalidExample.fix: the range is 1-based — start must be >= 1 and <= the end (start == end is allowed)

operators.meaning: A field's value coerced to its string representation — typically to compare against, or concatenate with, other strings.
constraints: the operand is a single field

validExample.note: fires when the quantity's string form is exactly 0

operators.meaning: A substring of a string field's value (by character range), read as a number — for numeric comparison/arithmetic.
constraints: the first operand is a string field; the two range bounds are integers — 1-based and inclusive, with start >= 1 and start <= end (MVK_INVALID_INTERVAL)

gotchas.text: a non-numeric substring (or an empty field) yields 0, not an error

validExample.note: fires when the first two characters are not a number (so 0)

operators.meaning: A string or enum field's value coerced to a number — for numeric comparison/arithmetic.
constraints: the field's values (or category values) must always convert to a number, else MVK_NO_CONVERT_IN_NUMBER (e.g. an enum whose values are all numeric)

validExample.note: fires for the higher rush levels (the enum's values are numeric)

operators.meaning: Resolves a partially known date field (a DateType with a date precision other than FULL) to a concrete date — the earliest (FirstDay) or latest (LastDay) real date matching the known parts.
constraints: the field must be a partially known date (date precision DAY_OPTIONAL / MONTH_OPTIONAL / YEAR_OPTIONAL), else MVK_INVALID_DATE_TYPE_FOR_OP
the second argument is the FirstDay or LastDay keyword

validExample.note: fires when the earliest possible date is after the start of 2020

operators.meaning: The day specification for ValueAsDate selecting the earliest concrete date of a partially known date.
constraints: only valid as the second argument of ValueAsDate

validExample.note: the earliest possible date is after the start of 2020

operators.meaning: The day specification for ValueAsDate selecting the latest concrete date of a partially known date.
constraints: only valid as the second argument of ValueAsDate

validExample.note: the latest possible date is before the end of 2030

operators.meaning: Constructs a date from day, month, and year (optionally century + 2-digit decade) operands — a comparable date. Components render as bare entity refs.
constraints: the operands must be bounded-integer / digit-patterned number fields (the kernel rejects a plain scale-0 number: MVK_WRONG_DATE_FORMAT_FOR_OP)

validExample.note: fires when the order date disagrees with the entered birth-date parts

operators.meaning: Constructs a time-of-day from hour, minute, and second operands — a comparable time.
constraints: components are bare number fields or quoted constants (Time("10", "30", "50")); a bracketed value [H] is rejected

validExample.note: fires when pickup is exactly 10:30:50

operators.meaning: Combines a date and a time into a date-time — a comparable date-time value.
constraints: the first operand is a date value (field, date literal, or Date(...)); the second a time value (field, time literal, or Time(...))

gotchas.text: a DATE_TIME field compares only to another date-time value (a field or DateTime(...)) — not to a bare string literal

validExample.note: fires when the scheduled date-time matches the order date at the pickup time

operators.meaning: The current date-time — the date-time sibling of Today. Compares to a date-time field, and (truncated to the day) to a date field.
constraints: discouraged with == (a moving target); forbidden in computations

validExample.note: fires when the scheduled date-time is in the future

operators.meaning: The model's configured base year, as a point-in-time. Polymorphic: a date (the base-year start) against a date/date-time field, or the year number against a number field.
constraints: only valid in a model that declares a base year (modelInfo.baseYear), else MVK_NO_BASE_YEAR

validExample.note: fires when the order date is after the start of the base year

operators.meaning: True iff a constructed date is real AND all its referenced fields are specified (Date(31, 2, 2024) is not real; an unspecified part also makes it not Valid). This is the date-construct overload (IDateValidityCondition); the custom-field-type overload Valid(field, "Type") is the separate ValidType entry.
constraints: the operand is a Date(...) construction (or a date)

validExample.note: fires when the entered birth-date parts form a real calendar date

operators.meaning: True iff a constructed date is not a real calendar date OR any referenced field is unspecified — so it is NOT the pure negation of Valid. The date-construct overload, distinct from the custom-field-type Invalid (see InvalidType).
constraints: the operand is a Date(...) construction (or a date)

gotchas.text: also fires when a referenced part is unspecified (not only on an impossible date) — so it is not Valid's complement; prefix AllFieldsFilled(...) to fire only on a complete-but-impossible date (runtime-verified)

validExample.dsl: AllFieldsFilled(BirthDay, BirthMonth, BirthYear) And Invalid(Date(BirthDay, BirthMonth, BirthYear))
validExample.note: fires when complete birth-date parts do not form a real calendar date

operators.meaning: True iff the field's value is a valid instance of the named predefined custom field type (e.g. "IBAN", "Steuernummer"). The custom-field-type overload of Valid — distinct from the date-construct Valid (separate catalog id). Operand 1 is a STRING or ENUMERATION field; operand 2 is the type name as a string literal.
constraints: operand 1 is a STRING, ENUMERATION, or EXTENSIBLE-ENUMERATION field (kernel message MVK_NO_STRING_OR_ENUM_OR_EXT_ENUM); operand 2 is a string-literal type name

gotchas.text: the type name is NOT validated when the model is checked — checkConsistency accepts any string (even a misspelled or unregistered type); a wrong type name only fails at runtime evaluation, because the predefined types are a runtime client-SPI (IPredefinedType), not a model-time registry

validExample.note: fires when the customer name is present and a valid EMail (the type name is not checked at model-time)

operators.meaning: True iff the field's value is NOT a valid instance of the named predefined custom field type — the negation of ValidType. The custom-field-type overload of Invalid, distinct from the date-construct Invalid.
constraints: operand 1 is a STRING, ENUMERATION, or EXTENSIBLE-ENUMERATION field (kernel message MVK_NO_STRING_OR_ENUM_OR_EXT_ENUM); operand 2 is a string-literal type name

gotchas.text: the type name is NOT validated when the model is checked (see ValidType)

validExample.note: fires when the product code is present but not a valid IBAN

operators.meaning: The element-wise sum of products across two parallel number field lists: Σ aᵢ·bᵢ (typically two wildcard repetition lists over the same group). Both operands render as bare entity refs.
constraints: exactly two number fields (or wildcard repetition lists), both in the SAME repeatable group (else MVK_DIFFERENT_GROUPS); the asterisk notates their lowest repeatable layer

validExample.note: fires when the stored price disagrees with the summed count-weighted line items (both scale 2)

operators.meaning: The first specified value over a repetition list, in row order; unspecified rows are skipped (a feldListenOp sibling of Sum). Returns the scope's element type — a number over a number field list, a date over a date field list.

gotchas.text: operands after the first filled one are never read (a formal error there is invisible) — but a formal error BEFORE the first filled operand suppresses the rule

constraints: a single field over a repetition list (a *-flattened scope)

validExample.note: fires when the first specified line count exceeds 10

operators.meaning: Constructs a date range from a start and an end date. Computation-only: it assigns a DATE_RANGE field in a computation operation; it has no condition form (the overlap predicates take date-range FIELDS, and a constructed range cannot be nested or compared). Both operands must be format-compatible date fields.

gotchas.text: operands are BARE entity refs: write DateRange(OrderDate, DeliveryDate), never DateRange([OrderDate], [DeliveryDate]). Brackets mark a field used as a comparison value; a function's arguments are not that, and bracketing them is MVK_UNEXPECTED_TOKEN.

constraints: computation-only — the operation of a computation that assigns a DATE_RANGE field; both operands are date fields with identical date format

computationExample.note: the coverage window spans the order date through the delivery date
